chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: When ride cymbals and the high hat came in
summary: Saunders dates the lowboy to 1932 and high hat soon after; early drummers like Dodds, Singleton and Krupa used snare shimmy beats instead of ride cymbals.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, when did guys start playing ride cymbals?
Well, like I told you earlier, we talked about it. Now, in 1932, that was -- there was a lowboy, see, and right after that, I would say, between 1932 and 1935, they started coming out with --
I don't mean the high hat, but, I mean, a top cymbal and riding --
Oh, riding, oh. Well, they've been doing that a long time.
Did you ever hear of Walter Johnson?
He's the first one I heard to play the high hat.
Yeah, right, well, see, that was quite a few years ago.
Right, right, right, right, right, right, right.
And I guess around then the guys started playing the high hat, too.
Before that, it was mostly the snare drum.

Right. Well, like, see, we explained earlier, that was that shimmy beat thing we used to talk about, that five-stroke roll. And Baby Dodds and Zutty Singleton, all that come out of the New Orleans type of drumming.
Krupa was playing that way for Benny Goodman.
He didn't play the ride cymbal.
No, no, no. Right, right, right.

Well, see, Krupa, when they were here in the early days, like when that Austin group and all that was going, and the Midway Gardens was going there at 60th and Cottage Grove. And all those -- but, see, guys like Baby Dodds and all those -- he was around them a lot. And so a lot of that wore off.
